The company grew quickly on the back of the 1981 film Raiders of the Lost Ark, was sold to Gap, and the Zieglers resigned in 1988 after falling out with Gap's founder, Don Fisher.
In April 1990, flying home to San Francisco from a conference on values-driven business in Boston, Mel Ziegler met Bill Rosenzweig, a younger entrepreneur. Over the following twenty months the two men and Patricia exchanged the faxes, letters and drawings collected here, and the Republic of Tea launched in 1992. The book was published by Currency Doubleday the same year with the subtitle Letters to a Young Zentrepreneur, and later reissued as the story of the creation of a business told through its founders' letters.

About the book

Over 20 months of faxes, Mel Ziegler, Patricia Ziegler and Bill Rosenzweig record how they turned an idea into a tea company. The Zieglers had already co-founded Banana Republic, and their letters with Rosenzweig capture the fears, doubts and daily breakthroughs and setbacks of creating a business. The correspondence covers inventing a product, drafting a plan and setting up a partnership, and the book reprints the actual business plan the founders used to raise money. The paperback edition, part of the Currency line, adds a User's Guide by the authors, an introduction and discussion guide meant to help readers put the ideas into practice.

BUY THIS BOOK

The Republic of Tea

Mel Ziegler, Mel Zeigler. Doubleday Business, $22.5 (314pp) ISBN 978-0-385-42056-3

More than a chronicle of the birth of a new business, this unusual 20-month exchange of faxes between the Zieglers (husband-and-wife founders of Banana Republic) and their partner-to-be, Rosenzweig (future Republic of Tea CEO), records with almost missionary zeal its authors' determination to convert a stressed-out, coffee-gulping society into serene sippers of tea--and make millions in the process. After much high-flown, often repetitious philosophizing, self-doubt and discussion of personal relationships, the trio finally got down to market research (in the U.S. and England), product development and the nitty-gritty of sales, promotion and operations. When The Republic of Tea was launched this past January, the partners soon realized that ``a business tends to develop a mind of its own that is independent of its founder.'' Illustrations. (Nov.)
